content.title: Tour of Flanders 2026: Route, start time, key sections, and riders to watch in the men's and women's road
content.text: Spring has sprung in Europe, but it’s not all greenery and blossoms. For road cycling’s finest, the season is defined by mud, punchy climbs, and bonerattling cobblestones – something they’ll get more than enough of at the 2026 Tour of Flanders. The second of the one-day Monument Classics races of the season, on both the men's and women's tours, will take place in Belgium on Sunday, 5 April. For the men, classics standouts such as defending champion Tadej Pogačar, Dutch multi-discipline star Mathieu van der Poel and home hopes Remco Evenepoel and Wout van Aert will all be licking their lips, with a route that promises to be anything but a cruise through the Belgian countryside. In the women's race, the local favourite and three-time winner Lotte Kopecky faces the challenge of Elisa Longo Borghini, herself twice a champion in this race, plus Pauline Ferrand-Prévot and Demi Vollering. Marianne Vos could also return, after missing the first classic of the campaign, Milan-Sanremo. Stamina will be key, and speed will be essential, as riders come face-to-face with some of the most feared, yet revered terrain in road cycling: the infamous “bergs” of Flanders – cobblestone sections that feature steep climbs. Tactics will also play an important role in the race, as riders jockey for prime positions in the peloton. Timing will be everything, as team leaders look for the ideal launch pad. Those in the best shape will hope to go the distance and cross the finish line first in Oudenaarde. Expect a thrilling battle from the sport’s top stars, and nothing short of a party atmosphere from the cycling-crazed Belgian fans, as the second of road cycling’s Monuments pedals into focus during the 110th men's edition, and 10th women's race, of the Ronde van Vlaanderen.
